Force distributions from sparse moving-camera observations

A 15-coordinate projected Matérn prior describes a smooth external load on a known material-attached spatial profile. The three models infer that load, fixed-amplitude internal SDE impulses, or both. All fit the same observed images per condition. The SDE-only model excludes external force: its zero external-force band is conditional on that exclusion, not evidence that the load is absent.

Inspect convergence before using bands. A nonlinear fitted proposal and Metropolis correction target the full image likelihood and standardized priors. Rank/folded Rhat must be below 1.01, both bulk and tail ESS at least 400, and no chain frozen. Failed checks leave scores and intervals provisional. This is one known geometry, with selected synthetic force conditions; no real-world calibration or inferred model probabilities are claimed.

Forces are measured in N and impulses in Ns. White-noise forcing is recorded as finite-step impulses; combined forcing is averaged over explicit solver windows. The spatial profile and temporal bandwidth are restricted by design. Camera, rest geometry, density and supports remain known. Full covariance and paired force/impulse samples are saved in raw run files.

Every retained state enters latent diagnostics, external-force moments, intervals and scores; the force-impulse functionals have separate diagnostics in JSON. An equally spaced subset per chain controls rendering and combined force/impulse evaluation cost and is not assumed independent. Compact coefficient moments and joint function draws allow querying the external posterior at other times inside the recording. Truth is used only after fitting for evaluation, including the force-basis representation error.
